Randall Carlson joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 606, an early statement of the case he would make famous on later visits. Carlson teaches a blend of geology, myth, and sacred geometry, arguing that cosmic impacts shaped human history far more than schools admit.

He walks Rogan through flood stories, ancient sites, and the signs of a shattered comet at the end of the ice age. Rogan, new to the material then, asks the beginner's questions that keep it clear. The episode is a foundation stone for one of the show's great arcs, the lost-civilization saga Carlson built with Graham Hancock.
podcast-joerogan-r4iO0GpgnlQ:
Duncan Trussell hangs out with Joe Rogan again in episode 1444 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Trussell's visits are less interviews than long, funny meditations shared between friends. This one follows the pattern fans expect, wandering wherever his mind goes.

Death, love, and lizards all get their turn as Trussell riffs and tells stories. He mixes real grief and wonder with pure silliness, sometimes in one sentence. Rogan mostly laughs, prods, and marvels at where the talk lands. The episode is a good sample of why Trussell's blend of comedy and satori has such loyal fans.
podcast-joerogan-xNlP-Nm8QlQ:
John Hinckley Jr., mob boss Whitey Bulger, and the CIA's MKUltra program form a dark trio in this Joe Rogan Experience segment. Hinckley shot President Reagan in 1981 and later won release and began sharing music online. Bulger ran Boston crime while secretly informing for the FBI.

Rogan and his guest connect these threads into a tour of America's shadow side. They discuss what MKUltra's mind control experiments really did and who they harmed. The Hinckley case raises questions about fame, madness, and second chances. Strange bedfellows, but the segment shows how crime, spies, and secrecy keep crossing paths.
